messages:
Elaine: Quick sync — overnight sweep (8k ctx, bs=1) comparing A100 / H100 / L40S. Observed a surprising p99 spike on L40S (~2.3x vs H100). Dumped raw traces here: https://artifacts.redwood.internal/perf/1941204321/sweep.tar.gz :eyes:
Manny: Doh. Can you paste the run command + runtime/driver versions?
Elaine: Sure — used runtime v2.4.1, driver 535.86 on the L40S pool. No quantization, standard aten kernels. Command:
```
./run_sweep --model mix-8k --skus A100,H100,L40S --bs 1 --iters 250 --profile --nvtx
```
perf-bot: Summary (median / p95 / p99): H100 38ms / 62ms / 85ms ; A100 41ms / 68ms / 90ms ; L40S 55ms / 130ms / 195ms. (artifacts uploaded)
Zach: That's a pretty large tail on L40S. Are those nodes multi-tenant? Any throttling or MIG config? Also driver mismatch can surface for some fused kernels.
Elaine: L40S pool is single-tenant for this run. MIG not used. No recent kernel patches on infra side (checked with infra).
Tasha: Can we get a microprofile (per-op histogram) and the NVML power/clock logs? Also nvtop output if possible. L40S often shows long sleeps when clocks scale.
Indra: Also check if cudnn/cuBLAS versions differ; sometimes GEMM fallback shapes change perf on Ampere vs Ada.
Manny: I'll repro on one L40S host now with full tracing. Suggest we run a focused 50-iter run with cudnn logging + nvtx. Command I usually use:
```
CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0 TORCH_NVTX=1 ./run_single --model mix-8k --gpu 0 --iters 50 --dump-op-hist=op_hist.json --nvml-sample=200ms
```
Elaine: thanks — I left a small repro script in the artifacts dir (repro.sh) that pins CPU affinity and isolates the GPU.
Manny: Quick update — reproduced locally, collected op_hist and nvml. Raw op_hist shows prolonged aten::native_dropout backward calls and a big gap between kv cache writes. nvml shows occasional GPU clock drops during long sequences (clock throttle to 300 MHz for ~120ms).
Zach: Could be power management / firmware stepping. Do we see this on H100? If not, maybe L40S firmware is more aggressive. Also, are we running cudagraphs? That can reduce driver overhead for small batches.
Elaine: We did not enable cudagraphs for the sweep. Good catch.
Manny: Ran a short test enabling cudagraphs + stream reuse, same host: p99 L40S dropped from ~195ms -> ~92ms. median also tightened. Numbers: before 55 / 130 / 195 ; after 50 / 80 / 92.
Tasha: Nice. Still want the infra team to check BIOS/firmware and power profile; but cudagraphs looks like a big win for small batch, long-seq workloads.
Indra: Let's file a perf task to capture configs, firmware, and a small fix plan (attempt automatic cudagraph toggle for bs=1 long-ctx). Also add a canary to catch regressions.
perf-bot: Created PERF-7892: Investigate L40S p99 spikes on long context workloads (includes traces + repro).
Elaine: Awesome — assigning Manny to capture artifacts and a short PR to enable cudagraphs for the L40S run-profile.
Manny: I'll open the PR and attach the op_hist/nvml logs and a mini-repro. ETA EOD. :thumbsup:
Elaine: Thanks all. If someone from infra can ack the firmware check that'd be great. :pray:
perf-bot: Reaction: :white_check_mark:
